title: Japan Buys Ukraine's SkyFall Interceptors and India Pushes Missiles into Central Asia
subhead: Tokyo signs a direct contract with Ukrainian drone maker SkyFall for interceptor UAVs, while New Delhi sells air-defense missiles to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan — two moves that show the drone and air-defense export map is rewiring fast.

sections.heading: Japan signs direct contract with Ukraine's SkyFall for interceptor drones
sections.body:
Japan's Ministry of Defense has signed a contract to buy interceptor drones from Ukrainian manufacturer SkyFall, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi told a press conference in Tokyo, according to a transcript of the Oct. 9 briefing and reporting by the Kyiv Post. The ministry is pushing for early delivery. Neither the contract value, drone quantity, model, nor delivery date was disclosed.

SkyFall is known for the Vampire strike drone (colloquially 'Baba Yaga'), Shrike FPV drones, and P1-SUN interceptors. Koizumi framed the purchase as part of a broader effort to absorb Ukrainian battlefield experience, saying Ukraine has 'accumulated more experience in new ways of fighting than anyone else in the world' and produces 'new drones with improved capabilities every two or three weeks.' Japan's former defense minister Onodera visited Ukraine in late September and announced Tokyo would experimentally introduce the drones.

The deal gives a Ukrainian drone maker a foothold in the Japanese defense market — a notable reversal, since Ukraine has largely been on the receiving end of Western arms transfers rather than exporting into a top-ten defense spender.
sections.whyItMatters: Japan buying Ukrainian-designed interceptors shows Tokyo is willing to import combat-proven low-cost drone tech faster than its domestic industrial base can deliver it — and that Ukraine is now an arms exporter, not just a recipient.

sections.heading: Raytheon lands up to $6.3B SM-3 interceptor contract
sections.body:
The U.S. Missile Defense Agency awarded RTX's Raytheon a multiyear contract worth up to $6.34 billion to manufacture and assemble Standard Missile-3 Block IB interceptors, with a base value of $4.43 billion, according to the contract announcement and Reuters. Production work is planned in Huntsville, Alabama and Tucson, Arizona. The deal covers five years with two additional option years.

The SM-3 is the exo-atmospheric interceptor used aboard Aegis BMD-equipped Navy ships and at land-based Aegis Ashore sites, using a kinetic kill vehicle rather than an explosive warhead. Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment Michael P. Duffey said the contract 'provides production certainty to our defense industrial base, breaks sub-tier manufacturing bottlenecks.'

The award extends the pattern of multi-year 'block buys' that the Pentagon has used to stabilize interceptor supply chains amid heavy demand from the Middle East and Europe.
sections.whyItMatters: Locking in five-plus years of SM-3 output is a bet that interceptor demand stays elevated — the same industrial bottleneck logic that has driven other recent missile block buys, and a signal that the U.S. sees no near-term letup in ballistic-missile threats.

sections.heading: India sells air-defense missiles to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan
sections.body:
India has sold air-defense missiles to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan, part of a Central Asian push targeting a region long supplied by Russia and increasingly by China, according to the Financial Express and reports summarized by MSN's news aggregation. The deals center on India's Akash surface-to-air missile system.

New Delhi is seeking new customers in a market where Russian systems have traditionally dominated, and the exports feed into India's broader goal of scaling its defense export sector. India has repeatedly set ambitious export targets and now positions itself as a lower-cost alternative supplier to Soviet-legacy operators.
sections.whyItMatters: India entering Russia's traditional Central Asian arms market is a competitive move inside the non-Western arms trade — it chips at Moscow's supplier role without aligning with Western blocs, and validates India's push to become a serious exporter rather than just a buyer.

sections.heading: Morocco in advanced talks for Israel's David's Sling
sections.body:
Morocco and Israel reportedly are in advanced talks over integrating the Israeli-American David's Sling air defense system into the Royal Moroccan Armed Forces, according to German defense publication ES&T, as reported by Morocco World News. The system — developed by Rafael and Raytheon — would complement Israeli systems Rabat has already acquired, including Barak MX and Spyder from IAI and Rafael, plus PULS rocket launchers from Elbit and ATMOS howitzers.

David's Sling uses the ELM-2084 fire-control radar and the two-stage Stunner interceptor, designed to engage ballistic and cruise missiles at ranges of 40 to 300 kilometers and altitudes up to 15 km, with a stated top speed of up to Mach 7.5. The configuration of any Moroccan purchase is not clear, and it remains open whether Rabat will proceed.

The talks sit within a defense relationship that has expanded sharply under the Abraham Accords.
sections.whyItMatters: If completed, the deal would push Israeli top-tier air defense into North Africa, deepening a post-Abraham Accords arms axis and adding a capability layer Morocco has never fielded — while complicating Russian and Chinese bids in the region.

sections.heading: Turkey's SSB signs €2.46B ASELSAN air-defense and radar contracts
sections.body:
Turkey's Defense Industry Authority (SSB) signed two major contracts with ASELSAN: one worth €2.46 billion for Hybrid Air Defense Systems and another worth $195 million for radar systems, according to SSB Bülten. ASELSAN also concluded a $125 million export agreement for weapon and electronic warfare systems to an overseas end-user.

The same reporting notes the HÜRSAT-2 space surveillance contract formalized between TUSAŞ and ROKETSAN at the 77th International Astronautical Congress, a successful firing test of Baykar's AKINCI UCAV with the ASELSAN MORFOZ guidance kit, and delivery of the ninth Denizhan-76 marine gas turbine for the eleventh Milgem-class frigate. Deliveries also included MPT-76 rifles, 120mm airburst munitions, 155mm concrete-piercing shells, and 2.75-inch rocket motors.
sections.whyItMatters: The ASELSAN awards are Ankara's largest single-day domestic air-defense commitment in recent memory and reinforce its strategy of self-reliance in the exact categories — layered air defense, radar, EW — where it previously depended on foreign suppliers.

sections.heading: Korea accelerates nuclear submarine and one-year acquisition cycle
sections.body:
South Korea's Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) told a National Assembly audit that it will speed up nuclear-powered submarine development, its three-axis deterrence system, and AI/unmanned capabilities, according to Chosun Biz. A separate Nuclear-Powered Submarine Program Group has been organized inside the agency, with plans to leverage existing submarine development organizations and technology.

DAPA administrator Lee Yong-chul said the agency will cut the acquisition period for some advanced weapons from two years to one for rapid prototyping. It will also push the LAMD long-range artillery interception system — the so-called 'Korean Iron Dome' — as planned. The agency also committed to faster F-35A and KF-21 fielding and an unmanned buildup.

The moves come days after North Korea fired missiles in what Seoul's military assessed as a response to South Korea's first domestic hypersonic weapon test, reported by Anadolu Agency and Reuters.
sections.whyItMatters: Compressing procurement from two years to one is the more consequential change: it is Seoul restructuring its acquisition bureaucracy to keep pace with Pyongyang and with fast-moving drone and AI technology, not just buying more platforms.

sections.heading: Iran's defense nominee pledges air-defense overhaul; BAE pitches microwave counter-drone weapon
sections.body:
Iran's defense minister nominee Mehrdad Akhlaqi outlined a 16-point plan before Parliament, pledging to restructure the Ministry of Defense, rebuild its industrial and production infrastructure, and develop capacity to produce new products within six months, according to Nour News and Press TV. Akhlaqi, a former head of Iran's Aerospace Industries Organization, said 47 years of sanctions had failed to stop Iranian defense production. A confidence vote is scheduled for Oct. 18; the nomination follows the killing of former defense minister Aziz Nasirzadeh in U.S.-Israeli strikes on Tehran.

Separately, BAE Systems unveiled a High Power Microwave directed-energy system at AUSA 2026, designed to disrupt or destroy drone electronics using ~99% commercial off-the-shelf components, per defence-industry.eu. BAE said the system reached Technology Readiness Level 6 and is configurable for fixed, towed, vehicle, and maritime use.
sections.whyItMatters: Iran is signaling it will rebuild air defenses through indigenous industry rather than imports, while BAE's HPM pitch shows the counter-drone answer is trending toward cheap, reusable directed energy as massed drone attacks — like the one that hit Riyadh — expose the cost limits of interceptor missiles.

bottomLine: Two exports define the day: Japan's direct purchase of Ukrainian SkyFall interceptor drones, and India's Akash missile sales to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. Both point to the same shift — the drone and air-defense market is no longer a Western monopoly, with Ukraine exporting combat-proven designs and India competing in Russia's Central Asia backyard. Raytheon's up-to-$6.3B SM-3 block buy confirms interceptor demand remains structurally high after the Riyadh airport failure, while Turkey's €2.46B ASELSAN air-defense award and Korea's push to halve procurement timelines show mid-tier powers industrializing faster than the legacy suppliers they used to depend on.
sources: Kyiv Post, Reuters, AP/WSLS, Morocco World News / ES&T, SSB Bülten, Chosun Biz, Anadolu Agency, Army Recognition, Nour News, Press TV (Iran), Financial Express, MSN News, defence-industry.eu
